src: Dixon Evening Telegraph, 9 Nov 1907, p. 4, note introducing the serial 'The Banditti of the Prairie' (Newspapers.com 77209483)

set.tovw: Lead grade D: county-history tradition of a counterfeiters' rendezvous; a 1907 retelling treats Bliss and Dewey as innocent, so the story itself is disputed
pinev: A 1907 Dixon Telegraph note recalls 'a robbery at Inlet Grove, near Lee Center, in which the robbers impersonated two citizens, Bliss and Dewey, these innocent parties being sent to state prison'. So one local tradition made Bliss and Dewey victims of the banditti rather than their hosts; the 1878 Ogle history's 'rendezvous for counterfeiters' is the other. Both are secondary.
